items.title: Robert Lewis Interview 1959-11-10
items.q: The interviewee does not respond to the interviewer's mention of Ori, nor does he mention Ori himself. The mention of 'Ori' and the incident with Ed Garland is entirely within the interviewer's turn.

ctx.x: Yeah, the drummer wasn't doing what he should have done, and Sidney, first of all, started stomping one foot on the stage platform to get him in time, and the drummer still didn't get the idea, so Sidney took the entire band, that's the walking band, around to the backside of the stage, which was open. Well, that's where the drummer was, and when Sidney got there, he growled furiously. I think the drummer came, too, eventually.

I was interested, because other New Orleans musicians I know, too, consider music sort of a form of communication, which it really is, and they'll talk. I think that fight between Ed Garland and Ed and Ori, Kid Ori, out in San Francisco, when Garland knocked him off the stand is when Ori said something to him on the trombone, a few dirty words or something, and made Garland mad.
Well, it's a very expressive form of music.
